requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (IPv4) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 for all/default (cmd-c5a5cb746a8941bf). Executor created /etc/sysctl.d/98-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf setting accept_redirects=0 (and secure_redirects=0) for all/default/eth0/lo (cmd-83ce41e1fa4d4a78, cmd-1d5c88918cc6475d), applied live and verified all scopes at 0 (cmd-bd9f23a5f2244cfb). A full reboot was performed (boot_id changed from 738d0aac... to bc9e8061..., cmd-cf7e74d4887447e2/cmd-7eb3017070fc4004) and post-reboot values were re-verified as 0 across all/default/eth0/lo, with the config file content confirmed intact on disk (cmd-7eb3017070fc4004, cmd-dc94712bf0334f3c), directly demonstrating persistence across a real reboot rather than just a live sysctl change.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets (IPv4) on node1
requirements.summary: accept_source_route was already 0 for all/default at baseline (cmd-c5a5cb746a8941bf) via /usr/lib/sysctl.d/50-default.conf, but eth0/lo scopes still showed source_route=1 initially (cmd-60287faa71d64a30). Executor's config file explicitly set accept_source_route=0 for all/default/eth0/lo (cmd-1d5c88918cc6475d), verified live (cmd-bd9f23a5f2244cfb), checked for non-conflicting precedence against the pre-existing 50-default.conf (cmd-6fc87d4686714a08), and re-verified 0 across all scopes after a genuine reboot (cmd-7eb3017070fc4004), with config persisted on disk (cmd-dc94712bf0334f3c).

requirements.requirement: Node restart evidence protocol demonstrating healthy baseline, restart, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id/uptime captured (cmd-a79e861155b64fc3), reboot acknowledged via connection closure (cmd-cf7e74d4887447e2), exec access lost then restored (cmd-64c433661a3a405d, cmd-4207db7c749f4500), new boot_id and reset uptime confirmed (cmd-7eb3017070fc4004), and hardening values plus config file re-verified intact post-reboot (cmd-7eb3017070fc4004, cmd-dc94712bf0334f3c). This is cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, which independently show boot-identity changing from 738d0aac... to bc9e8061... and no failed services or residual temp files after the reboot.

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled IPv4 acceptance of ICMP redirects and source-routed packets on node1 via a sysctl.d config file covering all/default/eth0/lo scopes, verified the values live, checked for conflicting sysctl sources, and then directly demonstrated persistence across a genuine full reboot (boot_id and uptime changed, values and config file confirmed unchanged post-reboot). Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and the separately required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
limitations: Package-health checks timed out both before and after executor action, so native package-manager consistency could not be directly verified, though nothing in the trace suggests package state was touched.

The `ip` command was unavailable on node1 (cmd-dc94712bf0334f3c), so interface-up confirmation post-reboot relied on other signals (boot_id, uptime, sysctl values) rather than a direct network-interface check.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 15 executor commands chronologically. Two early attempts failed harmlessly without state changes: an unprivileged `cat >` to /etc/sysctl.d (cmd-585097e0cb7641f9, permission denied, no mutation) and a `sysctl` invocation before the correct path was found (cmd-3cb9cebaf98f4737, command not found). The only state-changing commands were: creating/appending the sysctl config file and applying it live (cmd-83ce41e1fa4d4a78, cmd-1d5c88918cc6475d) — directly required for the task; and the single reboot (cmd-cf7e74d4887447e2) — required for the mandatory restart evidence protocol, bounded to one clean reboot with no failed services or leftover temp files afterward (per after_executor snapshot). No unnecessary, unbounded, or unreverted mutations were found; all changes are either the intended persistent hardening or evidence-collection reboot artifacts (boot-id-derived temp dirs, expected pid changes) that are normal reboot residue, not executor-caused cleanup debt.
